title: Uptime Orchestration Campaign Map and Cadet Instructions
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working campaign map for a 30/60/90 uptake program to align product, serving-runtime, platform-engineering, and SRE around a small set of production SLOs. It is meant to be an operational cookbook for the cadet rotations (engineers new to SRE on 30-day embeddings) and a coordination canvas for cross-functional partners.

High-level goals:
- Establish a single source-of-truth SLO set (latency P50/P95, availability by route, error-rate) for model-serving endpoints used by hosted API and Dedicated pools.
- Run three staggered cadet rotations to validate handoffs, alerts, and oncall playbooks.
- Reduce P95 tail by 15% for heavy chat routes within 90 days via targeted mitigations (batch tuning, cache warmers, fallback routing).

Scope:
- Included: hosted-api read/write inference routes, primary embedding pipeline, model-routing control plane, rollout/rollback paths in Console.
- Excluded: customer-managed Private on-prem instances (separate program).

Success metrics (dashboard-driven):
- SLO adoption: number of feature teams with SLOs wired into the Console -> target 6 by day 60.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for critical alerts during cadet rotation <= 5 min.
- Regression guard: zero SLA regressions after any canary rollback for the 90-day pilot.

Stakeholder map (primary contacts):
- Program lead: Ava Moreno (eng-sre)
- Serving runtime: Ethan Park (serving-runtime)
- Platform and autoscaling: Maya Li (platform-engineering)
- Product (hosted API): Jamal Ortiz (product-hosted-api)
- Observability: Sofia Becker (observability)
- Solutions/CS liaison: Priya Nair (customer-success)

30/60/90 cadence and concrete milestones:
- Week 0 (prep): nominate cadets, confirm route list, wire up a minimal SLO dashboard, smoke tests for alerting. Deliverables: SRE-612 (route inventory), linked Confluence page.
- Day 0-30 (phase 1): First cadet rotation: shadow oncall + runbook dry-runs. Tasks: run failure-mode tabletop, exercise fallback routing for model outages, validate KV/prefix caching for one high-throughput route. Deliverable: rotation-retro notes and list of 5 quick wins.
- Day 31-60 (phase 2): Cross-team handoffs: product owners sign off on SLO definitions, platform applies autoscaling experiments (burst policy adjustments), create canary-to-prod rollbook. Deliverable: canary rollbook v1 and two platform experiment results.
- Day 61-90 (phase 3): Hardening and handoff: embed SLO ownership into team weekly rituals, finalize steward rotation schedule, measure P95 improvement and incident drills. Deliverable: SLO ownership matrix and final retro.

Cadet instructions (quick start):
1) Pre-rotation checklist: read the SLO glossary (Confluence link in linked artifacts), join #sre-uptime-cadets, clone the monitoring playground dashboard.
2) Day-one tasks: run local alert replay for the selected route (use synthetic events), confirm runbook steps for alert triage, escalate per matrix if unresolved after 10 minutes.
3) Shadowing: observe at least two real incidents (or simulated) and log MTTA/MTTR metrics in the cadet journal.
4) Dry-run: perform a simulated rollback using the canary runbook in the staging cluster and capture lessons.
5) Deliverable for cadets: a 1-page play summary with 3 suggested mitigations and one doc edit proposal.

Runbooks and artifacts (links and notes):
- Minimal triage runbook: service-triage-minimal.md (on repo) — ensure the runbook has decision gates for routing fallback.
- Canary runbook v1: include explicit steps for model variant fallback, cache invalidation ordering, and rolling abort thresholds.
- Observability checklist: synthetic checks for KV cache hit-rate, request fan-out ratio, and tokenized latency profile.

Risk map and mitigation ideas:
- Risk: Overloading cadets with ownership before runbooks are mature -> Mitigation: pair every cadet with a steward for first 48 hours and limit blast radius (staging-only actions).
- Risk: SLO noise from test traffic -> Mitigation: tagging route traffic sources and excluding internal synthetic runs from SLO numerator/denominator.
- Risk: Rollout-induced regressions -> Mitigation: automated rollback thresholds + preflight API shape compatibility checks.

Open questions (to resolve in kickoff):
- Which exact routes are tagged as "critical" for the pilot? Proposal: chat-streaming, embeddings-batch, and reranker-topk.
- Do we include dedicated pool metrics in the same SLO dashboard or in a linked view?
- Who owns the cost impact analysis for autoscaling experiments (billing vs infra)?

Communication rituals and meeting cadence:
- Weekly SLO sync (30 min): cadet updates, dashboard review, experiment results. Invite list: program lead, cadet leads, serving-runtime, platform.
- Bi-weekly tabletop: inject one runbook scenario and run to completion.
- Ad-hoc war room: when error budget burn > 50% in 24h.

Next immediate actions (owners):
- Ava: finalize cadet shortlist and send invites (due 2026-12-08).
- Ethan: prepare the staging canary that supports fallback routing (due 2026-12-10).
- Maya: draft autoscaling experiment config and cost guardrails (due 2026-12-13).
- Sofia: publish minimal SLO dashboard and synthetic checks (due 2026-12-11).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider an "incident mini-hack" prize to keep cadet engagement high.
- Small sample of A/B batching configs can yield large P95 wins — target two quick experiments.
- Keep the cadet journal public (internal) so product teams can see learning velocity.

Appendix: quick references and templates (copy-edit before final):
- Cadet 30-day journal template: [date | incident summary | MTTA | MTTR | mitigation | doc edits]
- Rollback checklist excerpt: verify no schema mismatch -> pause traffic -> revert model -> revalidate canary.
- Contact escalation ladder: primary steward -> program lead -> oncall SRE -> platform escalation.

End of draft.

(If you’re reading this as a product/engineer: add route nominations to SRE-612 and flag any blocking tickets. This doc will be iterated rapidly during the prep week.)
